open_points.subject: publish_progress_photo and _classify_photo_replay photo_date handling
open_points.text: - publish_progress_photo: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself. A supplied `photo_date` that carries a UTC offset MUST be converted to UTC, keeping its instant, before it is stored offset-naive; a supplied offset-naive value is taken as UTC.
open_points.other_text: - _classify_photo_replay: [BEHAVIOR] MUST return existing only when the same intake_id publication content agrees: project_id, section_id, caption, client_visible, file_ref and photo_date are equal (intake_source is not persisted and is not compared); conflict raises PhotoConflictError without mutation, intake_id being the replay identity.
open_points.question: Must replay comparison normalize publication.photo_date to UTC offset-naive before testing equality, or must the requirement that the two photo_date values be equal change? As written, replaying the same offset-aware publication after its date was stored offset-naive makes the values unequal.
